The test image shows a soybean field with a distinct strip/band of yellowing (chlorotic) plants running through otherwise healthy green plants. Key observations:
- Interveinal yellowing/chlorosis visible on affected plants
- Plants in affected area appear somewhat stunted
- The pattern shows a defined area/strip affected while surrounding plants remain green

This pattern — yellowing in defined patches/areas — is characteristic of Soybean Cyst Nematode or Sudden Death Syndrome. Let me check the SCN reference image.

The reference image for Soybean Cyst Nematode (SCN) closely matches the test image:
- The top-left panel shows a field-level view with a distinct strip/zone of affected plants — matching the test image's strip of yellowing plants
- The top-right and bottom-right panels show interveinal chlorosis (yellow leaves with some green areas) matching the test image's affected plants
- The pattern of defined yellow patches within otherwise healthy green field is the hallmark of SCN

This is a field-level shot showing the "circular or lens-shaped patterns" of yellowing/stunting described for SCN, with the "yellow dwarf" symptom visible in the affected strip.
